rule: Languages without one (Ruby, PHP, C, C++, ObjC, Zig file scope) use the file path below the scan root without extension (`lib/devise/rails/routes`). | An empty caller or `<global>` is a wrong caller. | **Objective-C++ (.mm)**: C++ constructs follow the C++ rules (`Cls::m` definitions, member calls, constructors); message sends follow the ObjC rules.
notes: call_type convention used throughout this corpus: a callee that is a member of a type (`T#m`) or a receiver-qualified guess (`recv.m`, `.m`) is `method`; a C function (bare name) is `direct`. Objective-C++ allows dynamic initialization of file-scope statics, so the two initializers in app/globals.mm run code outside any function: caller = file path below the scan root without extension, `app/globals`. The macro invocations in the file-scope array initializer of data/tables.m have caller `data/tables` (two invocations on one line → two edges). In the class method `+make`, `self` is the Registry class: `[self alloc]` → `Registry#alloc` and the init runs on a Registry → `Registry#init`, both medium (inherited from NSObject, outside the scan). `computeCount` is a C++ function in the global namespace → bare.
